title: Decision log
tagline: What you chose, what you didn't, and why.
description: Tell your AI about a decision and it logs the context, the options and why. Ask it later why you chose.

Decision log

## Open questions
What still needs deciding.
- Do we support offline editing in the first release?
- Who owns the importer after the launch?

## Decisions
Newest first: the context, what you chose and why.
### Stay on Postgres, 4 November
- **Context:** notes grew to 2 million rows and search got slow.
- **Options:** a document store, a search service, or better indexes.
- **Chose:** Postgres with a trigram index.
- **Why:** one database to run, and the index made search 40 times faster.
- **Revisit:** at 20 million rows.

### Release every Tuesday, 2 November
- **Context:** releases slipped whenever one fix wasn't ready.
- **Chose:** ship what's ready every Tuesday.
- **Why:** small releases are easier to undo.

title: Book notes
tagline: The big idea and the lines worth keeping.
description: Send highlights as you read. Your AI files the quotes, then writes up the big idea when you finish.
ask: Ask which book I'm reading and what stood out so far, then start its notes.
example:
Book notes

What stuck from each book: the big idea, the lines worth keeping, and what you'll do differently. Tell your AI which book you're reading to start its notes.

## Books
One section per book, newest first.
### Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
> "The day will never arrive when you finally have everything under control." (p. 31)

- The to-do list is infinite by design. Finishing it isn't the goal.
- Pick your three big projects; everything else waits.
- Saying no to good things is the hard part.
- Rest isn't a reward for finishing: nothing is ever finished.

**The big idea:** life is short and attention is finite. Trying to do everything guarantees the important things get squeezed. Choose what to neglect, on purpose.

- [ ] Keep a list of three active projects, no more
- [ ] Do the most important thing first, before email
- [ ] Keep one evening a week with nothing planned

### Deep Work by Cal Newport
- Two focused hours beat a scattered day.
- Shallow work gets a slot of its own, so it can't leak into the rest.

**The big idea:** attention is the thing to protect. Decide when the deep work happens before the day decides for you.

title: Cornell notes
tagline: Your notes, a cue for each, a summary.
description: Your notes on the right, a question for each on the left, a short summary. Then your AI quizzes you.
ask: Ask me for my lecture or reading notes, then make Cornell notes and quiz me.
example:
Cornell notes

Paste your lecture or reading notes into your AI. Your notes go on the right, a question each one answers on the left, and a short summary closes the section. To revise, cover the right column and answer the cues.

## Lectures
One section per lecture or chapter.
### Supply and demand, 5 November
| Cue | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| What shifts the demand curve? | Income, tastes, related prices. |
| What moves along the curve? | Only the good's own price. |
| What is the equilibrium price? | Where demand equals supply. |
| What does a price ceiling cause? | A shortage, if it's below equilibrium. |

**Summary:** The good's own price moves you along the demand curve; income, tastes and related prices shift it. The price settles where demand equals supply, and a ceiling below that leaves a shortage.

## Cues to revisit
The cues you missed when quizzed, ticked once you get them right.
- [ ] What shifts the demand curve?
- [x] What does a price ceiling cause?

title: Daily journal
tagline: Four questions a day, written up for you.
description: Answer four short questions, or just tell your AI about your day. It writes the entry, newest day first.
ask: Ask me today's four questions one at a time, then write up the entry.
example:
Daily journal

A few lines a day. Tell your AI about your day, or let it ask the questions below, and the entry lands here, newest day first.

## Questions
1. What happened today?
2. What took energy, and what gave it back?
3. What do I want to remember?
4. What's one thing for tomorrow?

## Entries
Newest day first.
### Sunday 8 November
- **Today:** quiet day; finished the bookshelf and went for a long walk.
- **Energy:** low after lunch, better after coffee with Jonas.
- **Remember:** the bakery on the corner opens at seven.
- **Tomorrow:** call Mum.

### Saturday 7 November
- **Today:** helped Maja move; it went faster than we feared.
- **Energy:** the stairs took it, the pizza after gave it back.
- **Remember:** Maja said the new flat gets the evening sun.
- **Tomorrow:** reply to the landlord before noon.
